source.authors: Alexei N. Skorobogatov and Efthymios Sofos

summary: Skorobogatov and Sofos prove Schinzel's Hypothesis (H) for 100% of n-tuples of integer polynomials of fixed degrees ordered by height: an averaged Bateman–Horn estimate (Theorem 1.9) by Linnik's dispersion method, with two-point prime correlations over coefficient boxes from Davenport's Möbius cancellation (§3) and local densities from a Bernoulli model (§2). They deduce density-one Hasse principles for cyclic norm equations N(z) = P(t) and diagonal conic bundles, and a 56% lower bound for x² + y² = f(t) (§§5–7). 103 items (6 library, 6 planned, 91 missing) are routed to two proposed Part IIs (Schinzel averages; random fibrations) and to ArithmeticStatistics ST.0, AnalyticNumberTheory AN.2/AN.5, ExponentialSumsAndCircleMethod ES.0, SieveMethodsAndPrimePatterns SV.2/SV.4 and HeightsRationalPointsAndObstructions RP.2. Twenty-two findings are recorded. The main one: Lemma 3.14 is false for positive primes (E1), and the von Mangoldt function must be even on ℤ (E4); the proofs establish the both-sign forms, and the main theorems survive through the von Mangoldt count and a bound on negative values that uses A₁ > n.

items.statement: For fixed n, d_i ≥ 1, A₂ > 0 and 3 ≤ x ≤ (log H)^{A₂}: the mean over the box {deg P_i = d_i, P_i > 0, |P| ≤ H} of θ^Λ_P(x) − θ_P(x) is ≪ (log H)^n log x.

proofSteps: Each term of θ^Λ_P − θ_P is at most ∏_i log((d_i + 1)H x^{d_i}) ≪ (log H)^n, and occurs only at m where some P_i(m) < 0 or some |P_i(m)| is a proper prime power.
If m ≥ 2 and P_i(m) < 0, then c_i m^{d_i} < H(m^{d_i} − 1)/(m − 1), so the leading coefficient c_i < H/(m − 1). Hence at most 1 + Σ_i min(x, H/c_i) values of m have a negative value.
Averaging over the leading coefficient 1 ≤ c ≤ H: H^{−1} Σ_c min(x, H/c) ≪ 1 + log x.
For fixed m, at most O((H x^d)^{1/2}) proper prime powers v with |v| ≤ (d+1)Hx^d, each taken by O(H^{d_i}) polynomials P_i: a proportion O(x^{d/2} H^{−1/2}), negligible after summing over m ≤ x.

routes.title: Arithmetic statistics, counting fields and Selmer distributions, Part II: Schinzel averages over coefficient boxes
routes.reason: ST.0–5 provide height-family and number-field/Selmer counting infrastructure, but not positive-prime values of fixed-degree integer polynomials in growing coefficient boxes. The local evaluation laws and three matched dispersion moments require new layers, importing generic family density and Fourier/arithmetic suppliers.
routes.brief: Extend Arithmetic statistics, counting fields and Selmer distributions (ArithmeticStatistics). Import ST.0 relative height-family density; Sieve methods, prime gaps and prime patterns (SieveMethodsAndPrimePatterns) for quadratic-character bilinear input; Exponential sums, decoupling and the circle method (ExponentialSumsAndCircleMethod) for kernel estimates; Analytic number theory, zeta functions and prime distribution (AnalyticNumberTheory) for Möbius, Mertens, PNT and multiplicative means. Endpoint contracts are items 9,11–15,24–25,74,79 and 83–84. In particular for fixed positive degrees d_i and M, n<A₁<A₂ and log^{A₁}H<x≤log^{A₂}H, the desired average absolute discrepancy is O(x/√log x); for Schinzel tuples in compatible congruence classes the fraction with at least (log|P|)^{A/3} prime witnesses up to (log|P|)^{n+A} is 1+O((logloglogH)^{D−n}/√loglog H). Preserve the common input, positive primes, positive leading coefficients, coefficientwise congruence and exact normalization. Use the even von Mangoldt function on ℤ (item 28): Theorem 3.1, Proposition 3.8 and Lemma 3.9 hold for it, and Lemma 3.14 holds in its von Mangoldt form (item 34), not for positive primes alone (E1). Run the dispersion for θ^Λ (item 100) and pass to positive primes with item 101; this uses n < A₁. State Corollary 1.10 pointwise in x (item 15). Construct finite-field coefficient probability, Vandermonde fibers, G_p, c_p, γ_n, singular series, CRT counting, large-prime tails and weighted counts with the stated API/tests. Reuse the built Vandermonde and natural Mangoldt APIs. Distinct-prime claims require deleting the repeated-polynomial diagonals. Proposed files: TauCeti/NumberTheory/PolynomialPrimeValues/LocalModels.lean and Dispersion.lean. Import the Bouniakowsky and Schinzel predicates (items 3, 4) from SieveMethodsAndPrimePatterns:SV.4. Proposed landmarks: Bernoulli Euler factors; Schinzel on average; quadratic-character cancellation. No conjectural full Schinzel or fixed-polynomial Bateman–Horn theorem is a proved endpoint.

routes.brief: Extend Heights, rational points and obstructions (HeightsRationalPointsAndObstructions), importing RP.2 cyclic norm obstruction APIs and ArithmeticStatisticsPartIISchinzelAverages for fixed-degree prime-value statistics. Import Class field theory (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ClassFieldTheory), layers 5,6,10,12, for local invariants, unramified norm units, ABHN and strict ray-class splitting, and Global quadratic forms (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/GlobalQuadraticForms), layer 5, for Hasse–Minkowski. Endpoint 61 is relative density 1 of rational points among cyclic norm fibers satisfying the specified unit-integral local conditions at ramified primes, together with positive ambient coefficient density. Endpoint 67 retains the column-sum Brauer conditions for a product of generic polynomials. Endpoint 65 gives a positive proportion of integral affine norm equations only under the additional hypothesis K^(+)/Q abelian. Endpoints 80–82 give relative density 1 of locally unit-soluble diagonal conic bundles and positive ambient proportion for arbitrary nonzero diagonal coefficients, with n₁,n₂>0,n₃≥0 and all prescribed polynomial degrees positive; resulting points lie in smooth fibers. Endpoints 86–87 give the exact product lower bound and >56% for x²+y²=P(t), d≥2. They use the prime-value input of the Schinzel-averages Part II, with the repair recorded there (E1, E4). Build basis-independent integral norm forms, unit-open universal families, joint smooth local persistence, compact-image finite CRT covers, invariant matrices, character indicators and thin-diagonal removal. Preserve the distinction between affine integral solutions and integral points of the unit-open scheme. The real sign hypothesis and nonzero projective vector must be explicit. Suggested files: TauCeti/ArithmeticGeometry/RandomFibrations/Norm.lean and Conic.lean. Suggested landmarks: local congruence cover; random cyclic norm Hasse principle; conic-solubility indicator;56percent integral Châtelet bound. No unrestricted Brauer–Manin completeness is asserted.
